description: Landing hits (sword or gun) accumulates hit-count toward the next rank tier: 10 / 20 / 40 / 70 hits. Taking any hit causes a full reset — all rank progress drops to zero. High-risk, high-reward: rewards sustained aggression, punishes mistakes. Each rank tier grants a flat melee damage boost (+5% per tier, multiplies with Strength rather than adding). On-screen rank meter plus an escalating 5-stage face-portrait HUD element (calm → glowing red eyes at max rank).

Attribute | Effect Speed | Movement speed Strength | Sword damage — multiplies with Gnarly Rank bonus Dexterity | Gun damage Defense | Damage resistance, clamped at 90% max Flat XP per kill; flat level curve (Level × 50); +2 to all attributes per level; cap at level 30. stated_status: Done and verified — full-restart-to-Room1 behavior (room-progression reset and exit-trigger re-arming for a repeat pass) built and verified across both branch paths.
description: Health bar HUD with live color shift (green → yellow/orange → red) as Health depletes. Low-health screen effect: smooth-scaling reddish dim below 25% Health, fading in/out rather than snapping. On death: brief animation, input disabled, then after a short delay a full run restart — the room progression state resets to Room 1 (whatever room was active deactivates, Room 1 reactivates), the player is teleported to Room 1's actual start position, and Health and Gnarly Rank both reset to zero. There is no partial/checkpoint respawn; death always sends the player back to the very beginning of the biome. A brief post-restart invulnerability window prevents an immediate re-death standing in the same spot. Design rationale: a full restart-on-death (rather than a soft checkpoint) is a deliberate choice to give the run real stakes and make the branching room structure (Section 2.6) replay-relevant — dying late still costs the whole run, and a subsequent attempt may take the other Room 3 branch.

stated_status: Done, committed, and re-verified end-to-end after a commit-split reconstruction.
description: The first fully-proven AI agent in the pipeline (see Section 4.2). Generates short, in-character one-liners triggered by kill / damage-taken / environment-interaction events, displayed in a JRPG-style dialogue box (portrait + name label + text, bottom-left of screen, auto-fade after a few seconds). Voice: deep, rough, growl-heavy one-liners — not clever banter. No cutesy cat-speak; "meow" only as a short, aggressive, bark-like sound when used at all. Two-layer pacing: each trigger type (kill/damage/environment) has its own long cooldown (5 min) so the same type doesn't repeat too often, plus a short global debounce (~6s) so two different trigger types can't fire back-to-back and overwhelm the player. Pipeline: batch-generated via the Claude API → hand-curated (41 quips currently locked in) → imported into a UE5 DataTable → read at runtime with zero live API dependency during gameplay.
